subject: Post-demo: latency budgets & cost options for Cortex Health integration

Subject: Post-demo recap + ask: latency targets and traffic pattern

Hi Elena & Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time to walk through the Cortex Health demo earlier. High-level notes: the model responses looked great for triage prompts and the streaming UI felt responsive in our test environment. To move from demo -> pilot we need to lock a few performance constraints so our ops and pricing recommendations align.

Quick asks from Redwood:
- Confirm the latency SLO target(s) you want us to design to (p50/p95/p99 where relevant).
- Typical request sizes (tokens) and distribution of short vs long responses.
- Expected concurrency patterns: peak concurrency and steady-state.
- Whether real-time streaming (token-level events) is required for all user journeys or only a subset.

I attached the demo recording and a small sample payload file. Ben & Neha are looped for cost/perf options.

Proposed next step: a short technical deep-dive next week (30–45m) to review the prompt set and agree on a mutual action plan. If you can share target latency numbers and a representative payload sample that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Marissa

Date: 2026-12-02T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: latency targets and traffic pattern

Thanks Marissa — great demo on your side. A few specifics from our product/ops team: 

- Latency SLOs: our primary goal is 95th percentile under 250ms for short-turn responses (<= 60 tokens). For longer, context-heavy completions (300+ tokens) we can accept up to 900ms p95, but p50 should be <300ms.
- Streaming: yes — we need streaming for the clinician-facing typing experience in the primary triage flow. For background batch tasks (note summarization), streaming is optional.
- Concurrency: pilot expected peak concurrency ~220 concurrent active sessions with an average of ~45 sustained. During business hours spikes may reach 300 for brief windows.
- Payloads: typical prompt payloads are small (20–80 tokens) but context windows can grow when we include recent notes (up to 4k tokens). Attached a sample set and a short CSV with hourly traffic estimates.

Constraints: our pilot budget for inference compute/ops is roughly $12k/month. Also, we need SOC2-compliant handling of PII — we can discuss deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private) in the next call.

Happy to do a deep-dive Wed or Thu next week.

Best,
Elena
Head of Product, Cortex Health

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-03T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: latency targets and traffic pattern

Elena — thanks for the details, super helpful. A few immediate thoughts on levers we can use to meet the p95 targets while keeping the pilot within budget: 

1) Continuous batching + micro-batching window tuning: For short payloads we can batch aggressively with a small wait window (10–25ms) to improve throughput without materially affecting p95 for interactive sessions.

2) Prefix/KV caching: Cache repeated context (patient metadata, static prompts) at the request-router layer — this often eliminates 30–60% of token compute for common flows.

3) Model variants + quantization profiles: Recommend a quantized 8-bit medium model variant for the default path to hit latency targets; keep a higher-fidelity fp16 or 16-bit variant for critical or fallback requests. This reduces token cost by ~35–50% depending on sequence length.

4) Streaming-specific routing: Use a low-latency node pool (smaller batch windows, reserved capacity) for streaming-enabled sessions and route background batch jobs to cheaper pools.

5) Graceful fallback: If the low-latency pool is saturated, route to a slightly higher-latency but cheaper model variant while surfacing a subtle progress indicator to users.

If you can share a representative prompt set (real or sanitized), Neha can run an internal microbenchmark and provide a suggested config + cost estimate for the pilot.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + ask: latency targets and traffic pattern — initial config & cost sketch

Thanks — I ran a quick internal pass against your sample payloads. High level proposal to balance your latency SLOs and the $12k pilot cap: 

- Routing: Streaming-critical sessions -> reserved low-latency pool (small batch window, pre-warmed). Background jobs -> shared spot/ondemand pools.
- Model stack: Default: 8-bit quantized medium model (Q8) for the interactive triage path. Fallback: fp16 full model for long-form generation and for any requests that fail the low-latency pool.
- Batching: 15–20ms micro-batch window for interactive pool; larger batching (50–100ms) for background jobs.
- Cache: Request-level prefix cache with 5-minute TTL for recurring patient metadata; KV cache for multi-turn sessions kept for 30 minutes.
- Concurrency handling: Autoscale reserved pool to handle 300 concurrent sessions burst for 2–3 minute windows; provision steady-state to cover 220 concurrency.

Estimated pilot costs (very rough):
- Reserved low-latency pool (mixed GPUs, pre-warmed): ~$7k/month
- Shared background pool + token usage on quantized models: ~$3.5k/month
- Buffer for fallbacks / ops overhead: ~$1.5k/month

Attachments: I uploaded a CSV of latency microbenchmarks we ran against the sample prompts plus a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that outlines milestones, owners, and success criteria.

Next step recommendation: 45m technical deep-dive where our infra engineers validate the KV cache keys and batching windows against your real prompt set. I can bring a sample cost-vs-latency curve.

—Neha
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference
